Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

# ARC: 3x3 halos around markers inside 3-panels

## Trigger
A grid contains one or more large, filled rectangular regions of color 3, with some color-2 cells embedded in those regions. Separate color-2 cells may appear in the surrounding background.

## Transformation
1. Identify each rectangular color-3 panel and the color-2 cells that are embedded within its footprint. Treat embedded 2s as markers; do not treat 2s in the outside background as markers.
2. For every embedded marker, paint its full 3×3 Moore neighborhood (the cell itself and the eight adjacent cells) as color 1.
3. Restore/retain the marker itself as color 2; only its eight neighboring cells become 1. If halos overlap, the union remains 1 except at any marker cells, which stay 2.
4. Preserve all cells outside the union of these halos exactly as given, including the surrounding 3 panel cells, background 0s, and unrelated 2s.
5. Keep the original grid dimensions.

## Reliable implementation
Work from the original input grid when assigning halos, then preserve marker cells as 2. A simple way is to copy the grid, set each in-bounds neighbor of every embedded marker to 1 unless that location is itself a marker, and finally ensure all markers remain 2. Use panel boundaries to distinguish embedded 2 markers from unrelated external 2s.

## Pitfalls
- Do not recolor all 3s in a panel; only the 3×3 neighborhoods around embedded 2s change.
- Do not expand external 2s in the background.
- Halos can extend beyond the panel boundary into background; include all in-bounds neighboring cells.
- Adjacent/overlapping markers each get halos, while all marker centers remain 2.
- A panel may contain marker centers adjacent to each other, causing adjacent 2s in the output; do not overwrite them with 1.
